extracted.intended_audience: BlackRock clients, asset owners, investors, regulators, and other stakeholders interested in stewardship and proxy voting practices
extracted.subtask_description: Corporate stewardship guidance describing BlackRock Investment Stewardship (BIS) policies and procedures for engagement, proxy voting, industry dialogue, and reporting on behalf of clients invested in index equity strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiduciary duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiduciary duty is a foundational principle: as an asset manager BlackRock is legally required to act in the best interests of clients and focus solely on their investment objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voting determinations and stewardship activities must be made in a manner consistent with clients' investment objectives; BlackRock does not make stewardship decisions to pursue outcomes for society at large (that is the role of governments and policymakers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term investor perspective and financial materiality-based approach
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS conducts stewardship from a long-term investor perspective and takes a financial materiality-based approach focused solely on advancing clients' investment objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagements and voting focus on how companies create long-term financial value and on material risks and opportunities. Policies are applied pragmatically and on a case-by-case basis to further clients' long-term financial interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: BIS Benchmark Policies (structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The BIS Benchmark Policies guide BIS' approach and consist of: (1) Global Principles, (2) Regional voting guidelines, and (3) Engagement Priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These Benchmark Policies are maintained globally to provide consistent principles while recognising local market characteristics. BIS reviews these policies annually and updates them to reflect market standards, client and company feedback, and research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Global Principles reflect BIS' views on the globally applicable elements of corporate governance that contribute to a company's ability to create long-term financial value for shareholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Global Principles inform regional guidelines and voting decisions across jurisdictions while allowing for local market differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional voting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional voting guidelines explain how BIS Global Principles inform voting decisions in relation to common ballot items in each market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BIS applies regional guidelines to ballot items and adapts to local legal and market norms. The BIS analyst applies these regional guidelines as the starting point for vote determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement Priority: Board quality and effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS focuses stewardship efforts on the effectiveness of the board of directors, viewing a strong board as contributing to long-term financial performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement topics include board composition, director qualifications, committees, oversight of material risks, and board-level reforms that affect long-term value creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement Priority: Strategy, purpose, and financial resilience
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS engages on long-term corporate strategy, purpose, and financial resilience to understand how boards and management align decisions and capital allocation with the company's purpose and changing business dynamics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversations explore how strategy and capital allocation support long-term returns and resilience through business cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement Priority: Incentives aligned with financial value creation
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS seeks clarity in how compensation policies connect to outcomes and to the long-term financial interests of shareholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BIS finds it helpful when companies disclose the link between pay design, metrics, and long-term shareholder value; pay-related proposals are evaluated against this standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement Priority: Climate and natural capital
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS engages to understand companies' approach to and oversight of material climate-related risks and opportunities and how they manage natural capital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement covers governance, targets, disclosures, and the oversight frameworks companies use to manage climate-related financial risks and opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement Priority: Company impacts on people
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS engages on issues relating to how companies manage people-related matters that are materially relevant to financial performance, including human capital and human rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BIS assesses disclosures and oversight related to workforce, health & safety, human rights due diligence, and other people-related operational risks and opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yearly policy review process
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS reviews Benchmark Policies every year and updates them as necessary to reflect changes in market standards, regulations, client/company feedback, and research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review is rigorous yet flexible to allow continuous improvement. Changes are typically language refinements or local-market clarifications; BIS applies policies pragmatically on a case-by-case basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: An engagement is defined as a meeting with the boards and management of companies in which clients are invested to deepen understanding of business models and oversight of material risks and opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only direct interaction (meetings) count as engagement; letters are explicitly not counted as engagements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative engagement policy
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS engages individual companies independently rather than alongside other asset managers or owners unless collaborative engagement is permissible and judged to better advance clients' long-term financial interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborative engagements are only pursued where allowed by local regulation and where BIS determines the objectives independently, including with whom and how to partner. In 2025, BIS did not participate in collaborative engagements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four pillars of stewardship
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS' stewardship program is structured around four pillars: Engaging; Proxy voting; Industry dialogue; Reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each pillar has specific activities: Engaging with boards/management; voting at shareholder meetings for delegated clients; participating in industry dialogue to inform stakeholders; and informing clients via publications and direct communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proxy voting process (end-to-end)
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS follows a defined proxy voting process: (1) Onboarding, (2) Reconciliation, (3) Ballot creation, (4) Ballot reception, research, and issue spotting, (5) Review and engagement, (6) Vote execution, (7) Reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BIS onboards portfolios to the electronic voting platform, reconciles holdings, receives ballots via custodians/ballot distributors/proxy vendors, the BIS analyst reviews materials and applies regional guidelines, flags complex meetings for further research or engagement, executes votes, and reports to clients and regulators.

rubrics_metrics.name: BIS analyst review and escalation
rubrics_metrics.description: The BIS analyst reviews company materials, broker research, third-party data, and public information, applies regional voting guidelines, and flags non-straightforward meetings for additional research and potential engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For complicated or controversial matters, the analyst conducts in-depth research, may engage with company executives/board, and discusses issues with BIS colleagues, regional heads, and oversight committees as appropriate before executing final votes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of independent third-party voting service providers
rubrics_metrics.description: Per BIS policy, where applicable an independent third-party voting service provider supplies vote recommendations to mitigate potential conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party providers (e.g., ISS, Glass Lewis, Egan-Jones) are used to supplement BIS' research and to provide independent recommendations, particularly where conflicts may exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest policy and governance oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS maintains policies and procedures to prevent undue influence on proxy voting activities and has governance structures (including oversight by the Nominating and Governance Committee) to ensure accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BIS oversees service providers, uses independent third-party providers when necessary, documents examples of conflict policy application, and ensures oversight by independent board committees per listing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: BlackRock Voting Choice eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility for BlackRock Voting Choice (pass-through voting) is determined by considerations such as local market regulation and practice, cost, operational risk and complexity, and financial considerations including securities lending decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability varies by jurisdiction and product; BlackRock determines eligibility based on legal, operational, and financial factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: BlackRock Voting Choice features and client options
rubrics_metrics.description: BlackRock Voting Choice provides eligible clients with the opportunity to participate in proxy voting; institutional clients can select among distinct voting guidelines from multiple third-party providers and SMAs may implement custom voting guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The platform expanded over time to include additional third-party policy providers; client participation is measured and reported (e.g., AUM eligible and AUM exercising the option).

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate and Decarbonization Stewardship program eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Climate and Decarbonization Stewardship program applies only to funds with climate and decarbonization objectives and where the fund’s governing body has explicitly approved the program; SMAs may instruct BlackRock to apply the program to their holdings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is only applied where appropriate per fund objectives and approvals and is separately reported; it represented approximately $194 billion in AUM as of the reporting date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for supporting shareholder proposals on corporate political activities and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS may support shareholder proposals requesting additional disclosure and/or oversight of corporate political activities where increased transparency would help investors understand governance and oversight processes for material risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When BIS supports such proposals it is not necessarily endorsing every element of the proposal; each proposal is evaluated on whether the requested disclosure materially aids investor understanding of governance and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal taxonomy and classification standards
rubrics_metrics.description: BlackRock uses a comprehensive proposal taxonomy to classify proxy voting items into categories (management proposals: Compensation; Director elections; Auditor; Mutual funds; Other; Strategic transactions; Takeover defense; Board-related; Capital Structure; Climate and natural capital; Company impacts on people; and shareholder proposals with parallel categories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This taxonomy structures reporting and analysis of voting activity and aligns with client informational needs. Definitions for each category (e.g., 'Compensation' includes Say on Pay, director compensation) are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and regulatory compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS provides portfolio-level engagement and vote reports to clients, complies with relevant regulatory reporting (such as SEC Form N-PX), and publishes its voting record, annual report, and quarterly engagement statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form N-PX is filed annually to disclose mutual fund proxy voting records. BIS also makes stewardship publications publicly available on its website and provides client communications as part of reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence in industry affiliations and external dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: BlackRock participates in industry groups and trade associations to gain information and insights but does not coordinate votes or make commitments that would interfere with independent voting determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memberships are chosen based on relevance and effectiveness for clients; BlackRock may engage in industry dialogue to further client interests but retains independent judgment on engagement and voting decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on engagement to influence control
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS complies with regulatory guidance and does not engage with portfolio companies for the purpose or with the effect of changing or influencing control of any company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The firm references SEC guidance (Schedule 13G eligibility) and ensures engagement activities do not have the intent or effect of influencing control.
